newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: WTO ruling on banana quotas victory for Guatemala.
newsitem.headline: WTO ruling on banana quotas victory for Guatemala.

text.p: Guatemala could get its first chance to export bananas to Europe without restrictions under a ruling by the World Trade Organization (WTO) on the European Union's banana regime, experts said on Wednesday.
A WTO dispute panel on Tuesday confirmed a preliminary finding in March that the EU's banana import rules favored imports from mainly Caribbean countries and violated open trading rules.

"Guatemala has never been able to export (bananas) to Europe freely and without restrictions. This will be the first opportunity," Julio Vielman, a Guatemalan lawyer who has closely followed the WTO panel, told Reuters.

The WTO panel on EU banana quotas was created in May 1996 following a complaint from the United States, Ecuador, Honduras, Mexico and Guatemala that EU banana import rules discriminated in favor of middlemen marketing EU bananas.
"The ruling in Geneva definitely confirms the victory reached by the Guatemalan government and its co-actors," Vielman said.
The European Union has the right to appeal the panel's conclusions but Vielman said if it loses the appeal the EU will be forced to comply with the ruling.
"Appeals are pending so we don't know what is going to happen," Javier Flores of the Guatemala Banana Producers Association told Reuters.

Guatemala exports about 10 percent of its bananas to Europe. Approximately 89 percent goes to the United States. In 1995, Guatemala's banana exports were worth $138.6 million, the country's third biggest export product after coffee and sugar.
Flores said he could not comment on whether Guatemala's banana exports to Europe could increase but Vielman said "it is very possible."
